trends.what: A curated list of free public APIs for developers to use in their projects.
trends.why: It's a go-to reference for developers looking to quickly find APIs, making it a timeless resource that keeps gaining stars.

trends.what: An open-source platform offering free coding lessons, projects, and certifications in math, programming, and computer science.
trends.why: Its comprehensive, self-paced curriculum and active community make it a top destination for learners, especially with rising interest in coding careers.

trends.what: A massive collection of freely available programming books and learning resources in multiple languages.
trends.why: It democratizes access to technical knowledge, which is especially valuable as education costs rise and developers seek free upskilling.

trends.what: A personal AI assistant that runs on any OS and platform, designed to be your always-available helper.
trends.why: The rise of personal AI agents and the quirky 'lobster way' branding make it stand out in the crowded AI assistant space.

trends.what: Interactive roadmaps and guides that help developers plan their learning and career growth step-by-step.
trends.why: With tech career paths becoming more complex, developers rely on these visual roadmaps to navigate skills and job roles.

trends.what: A tool that makes AI agents adopt a 'lazy senior dev' mindset, prioritizing minimal code and avoiding unnecessary work.
trends.why: It taps into the growing trend of optimizing AI efficiency and the humorous yet practical idea of 'lazy coding' resonates with devs.

trends.what: A fullscreen, mouse-interactive coding agent harness and terminal UI from SpaceXAI for building with AI.
trends.why: It brings a polished, interactive terminal experience to AI-assisted coding, appealing to developers who want more control and visual feedback.

trends.what: A pure C, zero-dependency runtime that runs frontier mixture-of-experts AI models on existing hardware by streaming experts from disk.
trends.why: It promises to make high-end AI models accessible on consumer hardware, a breakthrough for privacy and cost-conscious developers.
